final_note: You worked through the key terms in Space.

concepts.def: The distance light travels in one year (~9.5×10¹⁵ m).
v = 2πr ÷ T for a body in a circular orbit.
A stable star fusing hydrogen to helium, gravity balanced by radiation pressure.
Late stages of a low-mass star's life.
The explosive death of a massive star, leaving a neutron star or black hole.
Light from distant galaxies stretched to longer wavelengths — the universe is expanding.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Space — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Space brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Space.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Redshift of distant galaxies is evidence that:
options: the universe is contracting
galaxies are heating up
the universe is expanding
light slows over distance

mcqs.q: The Sun is currently in which stage?
options: Protostar
Main sequence
Red giant
White dwarf

mcqs.q: Was the Big Bang an explosion of matter into pre-existing space?
options: Intensity has no effect on anything in the photoelectric effect.
No — it was the expansion of space itself, beginning from a hot dense state; there was no 'outside' for matter to expand into.
Yes — it was a bomb-like event that destroyed an earlier universe.
Yes — it was a giant explosion at a point, and galaxies are still flying outwards from it.

mcqs.q: What is required to induce an emf in a coil using a magnet?
options: Yes — it was a bomb-like event that destroyed an earlier universe.
A changing magnetic flux linkage through the coil — the magnet (or coil) must be moving or the field must be changing.
Just having a magnet near the coil induces an emf, even when both are stationary.
A current in the coil is what induces an emf in the magnet.

mcqs.q: How does the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons depend on light intensity?
options: It does not — max KE depends only on the frequency of the light; intensity affects the rate (number) of electrons emitted.
A current in the coil is what induces an emf in the magnet.
Intensity has no effect on anything in the photoelectric effect.
Higher intensity gives photoelectrons more kinetic energy.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Big Bang theory”?
options: The universe began as a hot dense point ~13.8 billion years ago and has been expanding ever since.
Explosive death of a massive star, scattering heavy elements made by fusion into space.
Light from distant galaxies is shifted to longer wavelengths because space itself is expanding.
A stable star (like the Sun) where outward gas pressure balances gravitational collapse.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Supernova”?
options: A stable star (like the Sun) where outward gas pressure balances gravitational collapse.
Explosive death of a massive star, scattering heavy elements made by fusion into space.
Light from distant galaxies is shifted to longer wavelengths because space itself is expanding.
Faint microwave glow from the early universe, evidence for the Big Bang.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Life cycle of stars”?
options: Light from distant galaxies is shifted to longer wavelengths because space itself is expanding.
The universe began as a hot dense point ~13.8 billion years ago and has been expanding ever since.
Nebula → protostar → main sequence → red giant → white dwarf (or for big stars: supergiant → supernova → neutron star or black hole).
Explosive death of a massive star, scattering heavy elements made by fusion into space.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Redshift”?
options: Light from distant galaxies is shifted to longer wavelengths because space itself is expanding.
A stable star (like the Sun) where outward gas pressure balances gravitational collapse.
The universe began as a hot dense point ~13.8 billion years ago and has been expanding ever since.
Nebula → protostar → main sequence → red giant → white dwarf (or for big stars: supergiant → supernova → neutron star or black hole).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Cosmic microwave background”?
options: Nebula → protostar → main sequence → red giant → white dwarf (or for big stars: supergiant → supernova → neutron star or black hole).
A stable star (like the Sun) where outward gas pressure balances gravitational collapse.
Faint microwave glow from the early universe, evidence for the Big Bang.
The universe began as a hot dense point ~13.8 billion years ago and has been expanding ever since.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Main sequence star”?
options: Light from distant galaxies is shifted to longer wavelengths because space itself is expanding.
Nebula → protostar → main sequence → red giant → white dwarf (or for big stars: supergiant → supernova → neutron star or black hole).
A stable star (like the Sun) where outward gas pressure balances gravitational collapse.
Faint microwave glow from the early universe, evidence for the Big Bang.

free_texts.q: What is the name for the explosion that ends a massive star's life?

sequence.def: Gravity pulls a cloud of gas and dust together
Collapsing core heats up before fusion begins
Stable hydrogen fusion, like our Sun now
Sun-like star swells once core hydrogen is spent
Outer layers drift away into space
Hot dense core remnant slowly cooling
